text: Get Help Get Help Find meals, shelter, recovery support and help with everyday needs. Do you need help right now? If you or someone else is in immediate danger, call 911 . This includes a medical emergency, fire or violence. For a mental health crisis or emotional distress, call or text 988 . The 988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline is available 24 hours a day. Si está experimentando una emergencia, llame al 911 inmediatamente. Si está experimentando una crisis de salud mental o angustia emocional, llame o envíe un mensaje de texto al 988 . Más recursos disponibles en 988lifeline.org . You can use this page for yourself or to help a friend or family member. Find meals, shelter, recovery support, a place to live while you work toward housing, or help with food and essentials. I need a meal I need shelter I need daytime support I want recovery support I need a place to live I need food or essentials I work for a partner organization Need help with Thanksgiving dinner? The 2026 Thanksgiving Banquet-in-a-Box program provides a frozen turkey and meal fixings for 8–10 people. Boxes are limited. Register and find pickup details on the Thanksgiving program page. I need a meal Breakfast, lunch and dinner are available to guests at the Lawrence Street Community Center and 48th Avenue Center. The Mission also serves meals in Northern Colorado through Fort Collins Rescue Mission . Where to go in Denver Lawrence Street Community Center: 2222 Lawrence St, Denver, CO 80205. Get directions . 48th Avenue Center: 4600 East 48th Avenue, Denver, CO 80216. Get directions . The Lawrence Street Community Center is not a public facility. It serves people who complete intake and use the Mission’s overnight shelter. At 2:30 p.m., the facility opens through dinner so people who have completed intake and need overnight shelter can sign up for beds. Call 303.297.1815 for more information. I need shelter tonight For men Emergency overnight shelter is available nightly for men experiencing homelessness. Sign up at the Lawrence Street Community Center to enter the bed assignment system. Go to 2222 Lawrence St, Denver, CO 80205 . Bed sign-up begins at 2:30 p.m. and continues through dinner for people who have completed intake. Ask staff about intake and bed assignment. Call 303.297.1815 with questions. The Mission’s facilities serve people who complete intake and use overnight shelter; they are not public facilities. For women and children Denver Rescue Mission does not provide emergency overnight shelter for women or children. Call 303.294.0157 for a referral to an appropriate shelter or find partner shelter resources from the City of Denver . In Northern Colorado Check Fort Collins Rescue Mission’s current service information . The location page reports a temporary building closure and provides updated shelter instructions. I need a safe place during the day The Lawrence Street Community Center offers drinking water, restrooms, meals and connections to other support in a drug- and alcohol-free environment. Staff can help you learn about long-term programs and other local providers. Evening access is listed from 2:30 to 7 p.m. and intake requirements apply to guests using overnight shelter. Contact the Mission before you go to confirm access for your situation. 2222 Lawrence St, Denver, CO 80205. Call 303.294.0157 . More about the Community Center . I want help with recovery Looking for outpatient treatment? Pathways of Life Recovery Services (PLRS) serves adults 18 and older, including men and women, with clinical outpatient substance use treatment. Call 303.953.3927 or learn about PLRS and how to get started . The New Life Program The New Life Program helps men who have experienced addiction, abuse or other destructive habits work toward lasting change. It is a free, residential program. What the program includes Bible study and counseling Education and life skills Work readiness and case management Participants work toward stable employment or equivalent income, healthy relationships, recovery from destructive habits, and sustainable housing. Some continue to higher education. Qualifying graduates may receive a vehicle or a year-long bus pass. Who can join? To join the program, you must meet these requirements: Men age 18 or older No sex offenses or current violent charges Physically able to work A 30-day supply of any prescribed non-narcotic medication Willing to take random drug and alcohol tests Serious about life change and open to the message of Jesus Christ What happens when I start? You begin as a program candidate at The Crossing in northeast Denver. You learn about the program, receive health and case management screenings, and participate in Mission activities. The live page describes an initial 30-day restriction to the facility, followed by a candidacy period that may last another 90 days. It lists eligibility for outside employment or school after approximately eight months and an overall program duration of 6–12 months. Ask the program team how the timeline applies to you. How to get started The online interest form is under maintenance. Call 303.953.3913 or email NLPIntake@DenRescue.org to speak with the program team. Check the live page for current contact and application options . I need a place to live while I work toward housing The Bridge program at The Crossing offers men, women and families experiencing homelessness a safe place to live while they work toward stable housing. What to expect A drug- and alcohol-free facility with random testing Monthly meetings with a case manager Life skills and educational workshops Program fees paid on time Counseling and a supportive community Income requirements Bridge charges program fees. At least one adult must have verifiable income of at least: $770 per month For an individual $900 per month For a family All participants must have at least $100 left after expenses. What documents will I need? Be prepared to provide these documents if requested at your intake interview: Photo identification for all adults Social Security cards for everyone in the household Birth certificates for children A marriage license or Common Law Certificate for couples One month of pay stubs or proof of other verifiable income; employment must be permanent A background check is part of the final application process. There is a wait list for approved applications. How to get started The online interest form is under maintenance. Call 303.953.3963 for information and current application steps. I need food, clothing or household essentials The Ministry Outreach Center helps people and families experiencing poverty or at risk of homelessness with food, hygiene products, clothing and other items. Food and hygiene items You can receive food and hygiene items once a month . Bring a valid photo ID. Clothing Clothing is available for men, women and families. Bring a valid photo ID. Sizes and availability depend on donations. Where and when to go Ministry Outreach Center 5725 East 39th Avenue, Denver, CO 80207 Monday–Friday, 8:30–11:30 a.m. The center closes early at 10:50 a.m. on the first Thursday of each month and is closed on holidays. Get directions · More about food and essentials Furniture Furniture is available only through case managers at approved organizations and nonprofits. It is not available directly to the general public . Case managers can request furniture through a screening and approval process. Call 303.331.2936 to learn more. Case managers: request furniture . I work for a partner organization The Commodity Assistance Partner program supplies approved nonprofits with clothing, food and hygiene items for people in need. The Mission is not currently accepting new Commodity Assistance Partners. Approved partners schedule pickup appointments at the Ministry Outreach Center, 5725 E. 39th Avenue, Denver, CO 80207, Monday–Friday, 10:30 a.m.–3:30 p.m., excluding holidays. Items may not be sold or distributed to partner employees. Approval requires an application and a copy of the organization’s 501(c)(3) determination letter. Check with the Mission for current partner status and application information . Helping someone else? Use the Mission’s printable Service Guide to share services, addresses and other details. text: Get Involved Join Our Team of Passionate Individuals Why Work at Denver Rescue Mission? Are you looking for meaningful work? Co-workers who treat you like family? We are a faith-based, non-profit organization in Denver and northern Colorado committed to bringing an end to homelessness one person at a time. Christ-Centered Work Hiring Now Every position at the Mission is an opportunity for ministry and is vital to the fulfillment of our mission. SEE AVAILABLE POSITIONS “I think that Denver Rescue Mission reminds people that God loves them. People who have literally lost all of the hope that they had.” MaDonna, Bridge Program Graduate “I think that Denver Rescue Mission reminds people that God loves them. People who have literally lost all of the hope that they had.” MaDonna, Bridge Program Graduate Meaningful Work With Great Benefits Meaningful Work Working at the Mission is more than just a job. Our staff members passionately believe in what they do and are dedicated to helping people in need change their lives, which in turn helps improve our communities. Caring Community By working together across all areas of the Mission, we are striving to make our organization a leader in how we care for, serve and mentor our guests, program participants and each other. Health & Wellness Your health and wellness are important to us. That’s why we offer generous health insurance options including an employer contribution to an HSA, an HMO plan with a FSA option, paid term life insurance, long-term disability and $1,000 adoption assistance benefit. Vision, Dental & More Employees can opt in for a dental insurance plan and a vision care package, and our Employee Assistance Program offers a wide range of confidential support, resources and referrals for every aspect of your work and personal life. Retirement In order to help employees plan for their future, we offer a 401(k) retirement savings plan with matched contributions at 100% up to 5% of your salary. Time Off Our employees enjoy nine paid holidays per year, including your birthday off with pay and an additional day off for spiritual refreshment. This is in addition to generous paid vacation and sick time. And after five years of service, employees can receive additional paid time off for a mission trip. Staff Development We see our employees as individuals and are committed to encouraging and assisting their learning and career progression goals by offering an educational reimbursement up to $1,000 per year. Rewards Every staff member receives a $25 gift card to celebrate their annual employment anniversary, and hallmark anniversaries for 5/10/15/20 years of service are marked with progressive rewards. View Our Full Benefits Guide Anti-Discrimination Policy Denver Rescue Mission is both an equal opportunity employer and a distinctly faith-based Christian organization. Denver Rescue Mission complies with applicable federal, state, and local employment laws, and strictly prohibits and does not tolerate discrimination against employees, applicants, or any other covered persons because of race, color, national origin or ancestry, ethnicity, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, age, disability, citizenship, parental status, marital status, political ideology, or current or prospective service in the uniformed services. This policy applies to all terms, conditions, and privileges of employment including recruitment, employment, training, and promotion opportunities. Based upon Title VII of the Civil Rights Act of 1964, the Colorado Anti-Discrimination Act, and the U.S. Constitution, Denver Rescue Mission has the right to, and does, hire only candidates who agree with our Statement of Faith and align with our Christian mission. Why I Love My Job? I love being an employee of DRM. I love to hear the stories of the guests, how they got to this point in their life, and the things they are working on to change the things that need to be changed! I love even more when they have been able to obtain permanent housing, and they are so excited to share that with me. I’m glad they feel comfortable to share that the changes are scary, but they are proud of themselves! Jennifer “I love working at the Mission because I have the opportunity daily to share the love and truth of Jesus with those whom society has rejected, ignored and often deemed beyond redemption. I get to pursue abundant life in practical ways with people, and I love it!” Angie I can honestly say I love what I do and even on those cold nights when it is packed at Lawrence Street, and people are not genuinely excited about the cold, the joy of those individual moments and the humanity that shines in these spaces, is a blessing every time! Jessica “The Mission is transformational. We get to see lives changed both in staff and the guests that we serve. Don’t be afraid to dive in. It is so amazing to be able to work with the guests that we do, and your path is open to whatever you want to make it.” Paula Where is Denver Rescue Mission? text: Get Involved Volunteer Learn More Learn More Thank you for your interest in volunteering at Denver Rescue Mission! Volunteers like you make all our programs and services possible, every single day. Meal service, mentoring a program participant or youth, helping sort donations, and more are all amazing things you can do volunteering at the Mission. Volunteer as an Individual › Volunteer With a Group › Find an Opportunity Meals Warehouse Support Youth Administrative Court-Ordered Community Service Education & Life Skills Special Projects Spiritual Vocational How Does Your Group Want to Serve? Meals Warehouse Support Have a large group, or looking for other ways to serve? Contact us to learn more . Learn More Volunteering Has Its Perks… Search for your employer below to find out if they offer any volunteer benefits. Some employers may even offer paid time off in exchange for volunteering in your community! Matching Gift and Volunteer Grant information provided by Don’t see your employer listed? Talk to them about what a volunteer or matching gift program could look like. Volunteer With a Group Groups of 2 to 10 people can volunteer for a variety of opportunities, but our greatest need for groups is in serving meals and assisting with warehouse support at our Ministry Outreach Center. Thank you for joining us to change lives together. Sign Up Your Group You Can Be a Change Maker Change Makers are volunteers who want to partner with us by investing deeper in the lives of those experiencing homelessness and poverty. Become a Change Maker Frequently Asked Questions What type of volunteer opportunities are available for individuals? We have three main types of volunteer opportunities: Short-Term: Serving meals, warehouse support, court-ordered community service, and more. Change Makers: Volunteers who serve on a regular basis working with adults or youth, teaching job skills, providing spiritual services, and more. Internships Fall, spring, and summer start dates are available. Use the categories above to find an opportunity you’re interested in. What volunteer opportunities are available for groups? Group opportunities for 2-10 people are available for meals, and groups of 2-5 are welcome to serve through warehouse support opportunities. Select the Groups category above to find an opportunity that’s right for you. Are there age restrictions for meal service volunteer opportunities? Age requirements for meal service volunteers varies depending on the facility where you are volunteering. All volunteers under the age of 18 must be accompanied by someone who is 18 or older (parent/guardian, family member, youth pastor, etc.). At The Crossing, the minimum age for meal service volunteers is 12 years old. At the Lawrence Street Community Center, the minimum age for meal service volunteers is 14 years old At 48th Avenue Center, the minimum age for meal service volunteers is 14 years old At the Ministry Outreach Center, the minimum age for volunteering is 16 years old. At Fort Collins Rescue Mission, the minimum age for meal service volunteers is 16 years old. Please do not bring family members or guests with you who are under the minimum age requirements for the facility where you will be serving. Who do I contact if I have questions about volunteering? If you have questions please contact us online . If you have a question about an opportunity or scheduling, please contact our Volunteer Services team at 303.953.3955 or the contact person associated with the volunteer position. How far in advance can I sign up for a meal service volunteer opportunity? You may sign up for meal service 45 days in advance. Select Meals above to get started. Can I complete court-ordered community service at Denver Rescue Mission? Court-ordered community service can be completed through select volunteer opportunities at the Mission. All court ordered volunteers must apply and be approved before beginning service. Please select Court-Ordered Community Service from the categories above to see available opportunities. If there is not an application available that means that the opportunity is full at that time. Can I bring my Emotional Support Animal or Service Animal to volunteer? Emotional Support Animals are not permitted while volunteering at Denver Rescue Mission. Service Animals are permitted. Volunteers who wish to bring their Service Animal should contact Volunteer Services at Volunteer@DenRescue.org at least one week prior to their scheduled volunteer date to complete the necessary documents. No animals should ever be left unattended in vehicles during a volunteer shift. What if my volunteer shift search does not give me results? If you are unable find a volunteer shift based off your search criteria it is possible we don’t have any available shifts that match your desired location or date. Once a shift is filled, it will no longer appear on the website. Shifts are typically released 45-60 days in advance. Please reach out to us at 303.953.3955 if you need assistance with scheduling a shift. Check your employer’s volunteer matching program on the Mission’s live website . News & Stories Stay connected. title: Denver Rescue Mission — Home
description: Through the power of Christ , working to bring an end to homelessness in Metro Denver and Northern Colorado, one life at a time .
text: Denver Rescue Mission One open door. A different future. Your gift can open that same door for someone else. Make a difference ↗︎ Looking for help? → Ending homelessness, one life at a time. Through the power of Christ , working to bring an end to homelessness in Metro Denver and Northern Colorado, one life at a time . Five connected strategies Prevention, Dignity, Recovery, Readiness, and Housing guide our work. Programs put these strategies into practice, and a single program can support more than one strategy. Prevention Sometimes the most important step toward stability happens before someone ever loses their home. Dignity A welcoming place. A listening ear. The respect every neighbor deserves. Dignity is the foundation of how we meet people, wherever their journey begins. Recovery For people navigating addiction, trauma, and other difficult circumstances, change takes time. Recovery is built through relationships, support, and the opportunity to move forward—one step at a time. Readiness Lasting stability takes more than a single opportunity. It takes preparation, confidence, relationships, and practical tools to move forward. Housing A safe, stable place to call home changes what is possible. Our work connects neighbors with support as they seek housing—and as they build a foundation for what comes next. Your Impact 627 Individuals Obtained More Stable Housing 93% New Life Program One-Year Success Rate in Housing 11,561 Unique People Served 604 Individuals Obtained or Improved Employment Read the Mission’s published impact results and financial reports . Stories of Changed Lives “I wasn’t expecting the level of support I got, simply because I know that because of my disability, it would take somebody who was willing to invest the time and expertise. title: Pathways of Life Recovery Services
description: Compassionate clinical care for adults working toward lasting recovery.
text: Recovery support Pathways of Life Recovery Services Compassionate clinical care for adults working toward lasting recovery. A path toward lasting recovery Pathways of Life Recovery Services, LLC (PLRS) provides treatment for adults struggling with substance use disorders and alcohol dependence. Guided by faith and compassion, its team brings together evidence-based care and personal support. As a subsidiary of Denver Rescue Mission, PLRS partners with the Mission to offer intensive outpatient and outpatient treatment. Clinical care complements the Mission’s broader work of walking alongside neighbors as they pursue recovery, stability and a renewed sense of purpose. Talk with the PLRS team Ask about treatment options, availability and how to get started. Call: 303.953.3927 Email: PLRS@PLRSColorado.com Hours: Monday–Friday, 8:30 a.m.–5:00 p.m. PLRS address: 6090 Smith Road Denver, CO 80216 Get directions to PLRS Contact Pathways of Life Recovery Services . Clinical care, tailored to the person Intensive outpatient care A clinical assessment helps determine whether an Intensive Outpatient Program (IOP) is the appropriate level of care. Outpatient treatment Outpatient (OP) services support adults with substance use disorders through an individualized treatment plan. Personal support Services include individual and group therapy, psychoeducational classes and case management. Care is shaped around each person’s needs, challenges and recovery goals. PLRS uses evidence-based approaches including Cognitive Behavioral Therapy (CBT), Dialectical Behavior Therapy (DBT), motivational interviewing and relapse prevention. When appropriate, the team coordinates referrals to other providers and community resources. Who PLRS serves PLRS serves adults 18 and older , including men and women. It works with people who have stable housing as well as people experiencing housing insecurity. Many clients are shelter guests or long-term program participants at Denver Rescue Mission and Fort Collins Rescue Mission. PLRS also welcomes inquiries from people who are not participating in a Mission service or program. How to get started Contact PLRS. Call or email the team to ask about services and your next step. Complete an initial screening. The team gathers information about your needs. Attend a clinical assessment. Staff determine the appropriate level of care and discuss a treatment plan with you. Do I need a referral? A referral is not required for most people. Referrals are typically required when transitioning from detoxification, residential treatment, hospitalization or the criminal justice system, including probation or parole. Contact PLRS to confirm the process for your situation. How much does treatment cost? Cost depends on insurance coverage and ability to pay. PLRS discusses insurance, financial responsibility and available payment or financial-assistance options during intake, on a case-by-case basis. How long does treatment last? Treatment is individualized. Length of care depends on clinical needs, progress and recovery goals. The team will discuss the plan and continuing support with you. Where will I receive care? PLRS is located at 6090 Smith Road, Denver, CO 80216 . Services may also be provided at approved partner or community locations, as appropriate. Find current contact information . Read the PLRS frequently asked questions . Recovery is part of a connected path Recovery looks different for every person. Clinical treatment is one kind of support; the Mission’s connected strategies also recognize the importance of dignity, readiness, housing and prevention. Explore our programs → A connected approach See the person, not just the circumstance. Dignity isn't something people have to earn. It's something we recognize from the first hello. Experiencing homelessness can mean facing uncertainty, isolation, and difficult decisions. Respectful, person-centered support can help a neighbor feel seen while finding ways to address immediate needs. For Denver Rescue Mission, Dignity is a core strategy woven through how we welcome, listen, connect, and serve—not the name of any one program. Be heard Listening before assuming. Making room for each person's goals, concerns, and next steps. Feel welcome Creating spaces where people can encounter safety, consistency, and human connection. Be respected Offering compassionate care while recognizing individual choice and personal worth. Connection begins with care What dignity looks like Small moments can change the experience of a difficult day. There may be no single formula for meeting someone with dignity, but the way a person is welcomed matters. The following examples illustrate the kinds of everyday practices that shape a respectful environment. 01 A personal welcome A greeting that recognizes the person, not a label or circumstance. 02 A clear next step Useful information about what services may be available and where to go. 03 Room for choice A conversation that respects individual needs and decisions. 04 Consistent care Following through with kindness and practical support. Why dignity matters Trust is built one interaction at a time. A meal, a safe place to spend time, and a conversation may address immediate needs. The experience of being treated with care can also make it easier to build relationships and explore further support. Real change begins when someone knows they are seen and valued. Understand prevention ↘ Looking for help? ↗︎ A STRATEGY FOR LASTING STABILITY How the five strategies connect A strategy and a program Prevention is a Mission-wide strategy: addressing risks before they become homelessness. The Prevention Program is a specific way Denver Rescue Mission puts that broader strategy into practice. Prevention also connects to dignity, readiness, recovery and housing. Explore our programs → A connected approach Stability is worth protecting. When a neighbor faces a setback, the right support at the right moment can change what happens next. For a family living paycheck to paycheck, a missed shift, an unexpected repair, or a sudden change in circumstances can threaten the stability they've worked hard to build. Prevention is the work of recognizing that risk early, connecting people with practical help, and making room for a different outcome. It is one part of Denver Rescue Mission's wider continuum of support. Act early Address a difficult situation before it becomes a larger crisis. See the whole person Recognize that housing concerns often intersect with relationships, health, and everyday needs. Strengthen stability Support practical next steps that can help households regain their footing. Understanding the challenge A housing crisis rarely begins all at once. The signs may be small at first. Early support can create more options before instability grows. The moments before a crisis 01 A sudden financial setback An unexpected expense, income change, or missed paycheck disrupts a household budget. 02 Hard choices follow Essentials begin to compete with one another, creating pressure around rent, utilities, transportation, or groceries. 03 Options become narrower Without timely support, a temporary disruption can become more difficult to resolve. 04 Support changes the equation Practical resources, connection, and individualized guidance may help a neighbor stabilize. The purpose of prevention Help people stay where stability can grow. Prevention is not simply about responding to an emergency. It's about preserving the progress people have already made and helping create the conditions for continued independence. A single difficult season should not have to determine someone's future. How prevention works Practical support. Personal connection. A path forward. The exact form of assistance depends on individual circumstances, available resources, and program eligibility. These examples illustrate the strategy, not a promise of specific assistance. 01 Listen and understand Begin with the person, not just the problem. Understanding the circumstances helps identify what is creating instability and what would make the greatest difference. Common questions ↗︎ 02 Connect with resources Practical assistance and referrals can help households navigate immediate pressures while considering available options for greater stability. Explore related programs ↗︎ 03 Support the next step Follow-through matters. The goal is to help neighbors build on existing strengths and move toward stability that lasts beyond a single moment. Prevention connects with other strategies—from Dignity and Recovery to Readiness and Housing—as circumstances change. title: Give Cryptocurrency
description: Denver Rescue Mission is now accepting donations of cryptocurrency thanks to our secure, online donation platform provided by our friends at Engiven.
text: Ways To Give Donate Cryptocurrency Denver Rescue Mission is now accepting donations of cryptocurrency thanks to our secure, online donation platform provided by our friends at Engiven. Donate Cryptocurrency Today Frequently Asked Questions About Donating Cryptocurrency What is cryptocurrency? Cryptocurrency, also known as virtual currency or “Crypto,” is a digital asset designed to function as an alternative to traditional currencies (U.S. dollars, for example) whereby transactions between two parties are verified through a public, distributed ledger, also known as a blockchain. Most people think of Bitcoin or Ethereum when they hear the word “Crypto,” and while they are currently the most widely followed, there are thousands of unique cryptocurrencies in existence today. What is the Engiven platform? The Engiven platform is a third-party vendor provided donation software technology that enables nonprofits to safely and securely receive cryptocurrency donations and then convert those donations into usable fiat currency such as U.S. dollars. Learn more about Engiven here. Denver Rescue Mission established a relationship with Engiven in September 2021, and currently accepts 39 different types of cryptocurrencies through our crypto donation portal here. Do I need to establish an account with Engiven to make a gift of cryptocurrency to Denver Rescue Mission? No. Donors will not need an account with Engiven. Simply visit our cryptocurrency donation page and follow the prompts to complete your donation. Is it legal for Denver Rescue Mission to accept donations of cryptocurrency? Yes. It is lawful for a nonprofit to accept a donation in the form of a cryptocurrency. On March 2014, the United States Internal Revenue Service (IRS) ruled that Bitcoin is treated as property for tax purposes (IRS Notice 2014-21). How are cryptocurrency donations treated for federal tax purposes? For U.S. tax purposes, transactions using virtual currency must be reported in U.S. dollars. Therefore, taxpayers will be required to determine the fair market value of virtual currency in U.S. dollars as of the date of donation. If a virtual currency is listed on an exchange and the exchange rate is established by market supply and demand, the fair market value of the virtual currency is determined by converting the virtual currency into U.S. dollars (or into another real currency which in turn can be converted into U.S. dollars) at the exchange rate, in a reasonable manner that is consistently applied. Donors who give cryptocurrency donations to Denver Rescue Mission will receive an electronic donation receipt (through the Engiven donation platform) in U.S. dollars with comprehensive details about each transaction. What will I need after I donate cryptocurrency in order to deduct the gift on my taxes? First, if you wish to deduct the donation on your taxes, you must include your name, email and mailing address on the giving form so Denver Rescue Mission can send you the proper paperwork. For crypto donations valued over $250, a standard noncash donation receipt from Denver Rescue Mission will be required. An electronic version will be sent to you immediately once the donation has been completed, and the Mission will also send a printed version in the mail. For crypto donations valued over $500, you also must file Form 8283 (Noncash Charitable Contributions) . For crypto donations valued over $5,000, it will be your responsibility to receive a qualified appraisal prepared by a qualified appraiser, and have him/her sign Form 8283 (Noncash Charitable Contributions) . A signature from a representative from Denver Rescue Mission is also required on Form 8283 for a gift of this size. Soon after you make your gift, the Mission will mail a printed noncash donation receipt with further instructions. Please Note: Cryptocurrency donated to Denver Rescue Mission is liquidated immediately after it is received. The value listed on your receipt will be the amount the Mission realizes upon sale of your donated coins. According to the IRS, determining final value of a cryptocurrency donation for tax purposes is the responsibility of the donor. Is the process of giving cryptocurrency safe and secure? As with any form of electronic payment or transaction, there are risks, however, our vendor Engiven has created certain safeguards they believe are needed to ensure that the transaction is secure. With the transfer of cryptocurrency from donor to nonprofit, Engiven believes the transaction can actually be more secure than many other forms of payment, provided certain protocols are followed: 1) By using the Engiven platform, both the nonprofit and the donor are required to undergo a simple but effective Know Your Customer (KYC) and Anti-Money Laundering (AML) screening which provides a high level of background security to ensure both parties are properly screened. 2) As with any cryptocurrency transaction, when transferring your tokens to Denver Rescue Mission’s wallet to make a donation, do not expose or share your wallet’s private keys at any time. I understand the value of cryptocurrency is extremely volatile. What does the Mission do with donated crypto coins? Engiven has been instructed to immediately liquidate cryptocurrency donations to Denver Rescue Mission. DRM receives the cash proceeds in our checking account within a few business days. How can I designate my gift to a specific program or service? If you would like to designate your cryptocurrency gift to a specific Denver Rescue Mission program, please contact Brad Jessen, Director of Philanthropy, at 303.313.2491 or contact Brad online . Will my cryptocurrency donation be eligible for Homeless Contribution Tax Credit? Yes, as long as your cryptocurrency donation is valued at $5,000 or more and is made before the Mission exhausts its annual allocation of credits from the State, it is eligible for the Homeless Contribution Tax Credit program. Similar to a gift of stock, it will receive 25% credit. Learn more about the Homeless Contribution Tax Credit Program here . Donate cryptocurrency on the Mission’s live website . text: Ways To Give Donor Advised Funds Donor-Advised Funds (DAFs) have quickly become one of America’s most popular tools for charitable giving. DAFs are like your own private foundation without any of the administrative red tape. One of the simplest ways to give real estate, stocks, mutual funds, or commodities, DAFs offer an immediate tax deduction for the market value of your donation, but also allow you time to decide when you want to give. Once you contribute to your DAF, the funds are invested, potentially growing over time. Then, you have the privilege of directing grants to your favorite charitable organizations, like Denver Rescue Mission. Benefits of a Donor-Advised Fund: Tax Benefits When you contribute to a DAF, you receive an immediate tax deduction, which can be incredibly advantageous for your financial planning. Simplified Giving A DAF streamlines the giving process, making it easy and efficient to support multiple charitable causes without the hassle of managing multiple donations. Privacy and Flexibility With the flexibility of anonymous giving, a DAF allows you to support the Mission while maintaining your privacy. You also have the freedom to recommend grants whenever it’s most meaningful to you. Investment Growth Your contributions can grow through investments, allowing you to give more to the causes you’re passionate about. Cost Effective A DAF is a simpler and less expensive option compared to establishing a private foundation for those who wish to manage their charitable giving. Long-Term Planning A DAF allows you to establish a giving strategy that extends beyond your lifetime. You can designate beneficiaries who will continue your philanthropic legacy in the future. *Graphic from DAF Direct . Did You Know If your Donor Advised Fund is marked as anonymous, Denver Rescue Mission does not receive any details about who made a gift to the Mission. We know that the work at the Mission could not happen without your generosity, and we want to share the amazing impact that happens through you. If you can ensure your DAF gifts are recognizable and not selected as anonymous, that helps us ensure you are thanked and connected to this work directly. Additionally, Denver Rescue Mission does not publicly recognize or publish any donor details in any way, all donations are for internal use only. If you would like to ensure your donation is anonymous but have submitted a grant through your DAF, please contact our representative, Michel, at 303-313-2460 or by contacting us here. text: Ways To Give Qualified Charitable Distributions (QCDs) QCDs let you donate directly from your IRA to Denver Rescue Mission while reducing your taxable income. Even if you take the standard deduction, you can still benefit from tax savings. Notify Us Of Your Gift How It Works To qualify for a QCD: Be age 70 ½ or older (must wait 6 months after your 70th birthday) Transfer directly from a traditional IRA to Denver Rescue Mission Give up to $111,000 annually (spouses can each give $111,000) Make outright gifts only (no donor-advised funds, charitable trusts, or gift annuities) Note: 401k, 403b, SEP, and other retirement plans don’t qualify. Consider rolling funds into a traditional IRA first. Tax Benefits: Excluded from your gross income (reduces your AGI) Counts toward your Required Minimum Distribution No charitable deduction needed or allowed Example: Mary, age 71, transfers $15,000 directly from her IRA to Denver Rescue Mission. Result: She pays no income tax on that $15,000, it counts toward her RMD, and Denver Rescue Mission receives the full amount. Please ask your financial institution to use the following address to ensure your gift arrives correctly: Denver Rescue Mission PO Box 5206 Denver, CO 80217 Additional Considerations State taxes vary: Some states tax QCDs as income, others follow federal rules. Consult your tax advisor about your state’s treatment. Eligible charities: Must be 501(c)(3) organizations like Denver Rescue Mission. Year-end deadline: Ensure your IRA administrator completes the transfer by December 31 for current-year benefits. Consult your tax advisor to learn more about making a qualified charitable distribution . How to Make Your QCD Step 1 Contact Your IRA Administrator Contact your IRA administrator to initiate a direct transfer. Download this IRA donation letter of intent to get started. Step 2 Specify this is a QCD for tax reporting Be sure to tell your IRA administrator that this is a Qualified Charitable Distribution for tax reporting purposes. Step 3 Notify the Mission of Your IRA Gift Use the form below to let us know about your gift. Anonymous gifts make it harder for us to thank and report on giving. Step 4 Keep Documentation for Your Tax Records For tax purposes, keep a copy of all these documents and the receipt we’ll send you once you notify us of your gift. title: Legacy Giving
description: Many people are thrilled to discover that including a gift to the Mission in their Will, or other planned giving options, can significantly impact the lives of people in need for eternity.
text: Ways To Give Join the Goodheart Society Your legacy donation will change lives for years to come. Many people are thrilled to discover that including a gift to the Mission in their Will, or other planned giving options, can significantly impact the lives of people in need for eternity. Join the Goodheart Society The Goodheart Society recognizes those individuals who have made estate plans or established life-income gifts to benefit Denver Rescue Mission. The Goodheart Society name honors the late Jim Goodheart, a former Mission guest who went on to serve as the Mission’s Director from 1909 to 1930. Goodheart Society members receive invitations to exclusive events and volunteer opportunities, as well as special updates from Mission leadership. Jim Goodheart became the Mission Director in 1909. Each legacy gift represents an ongoing commitment to partner with the Mission to change lives in the name of Christ, therefore there is no minimum donation size for membership in the Goodheart Society . Individuals are not required to disclose the size of their legacy commitment, however the Mission welcomes members to do so in order to facilitate good stewardship and planning for the future. Goodheart Society member names are not printed in any listing available to the public. Members can request higher levels of anonymity if desired. Already have a gift to the Mission set up in your will? Let us know about it here. Create a Will Today Other Charitable Giving Tools Notice of Bequest Formstack Form Here Learn More About Giving from Your Will Writing an Ethical Will An Ethical Will is a personal document you write in order to help you pass on your beliefs, values and more to your loved ones. Writing an Ethical Will An “Ethical Will” (sometimes referred to as a “Legacy Love Letter”) is a document that traces its origins to Genesis 49:1-33, when a dying Jacob gathered his sons to offer them his blessing. Because an Ethical Will is not a legal document and is not made for the purpose of distributing assets, the content and form of your letter is up to you. Here are three themes you may wish to cover in your Ethical Will: Beliefs and Values: What do you believe about God? What are your guiding principles when it comes to marriage, raising children, church and ministry, handling money, etc. Life Lessons: What were some of the defining moments of your life, and what did you learn from them? What experiences and people are you most grateful for? Message of Hope: What are some of the most meaningful passages of Scripture to you? What message of hope and encouragement do you wish to leave to your family and friends? DOWNLOAD SAMPLE Learn More Important Documents Help your loved ones to find the information they’ll need when the time comes by gathering these important documents. Important Documents Make it easy for your loved ones to locate the documents they’ll need when the time comes with a Legacy File that includes the following: Duplicate Copy: If you create a duplicate copy of your Legacy File for your executor and for a safe deposit box, you should provide contact and location information. Finances: Provide a list of bank accounts, CDs, mutual funds, and other investments with institution names, account names and account numbers. Funeral Instructions: Provide details about your wishes for the funeral service, funeral home, burial arrangements. Important Documents: Create a “catchall” file for all other important documents your family may need such as birth certificates, Social Security cards, titles, etc. Insurance: Create a single file with all insurance information—including auto, home, life, health, disability, etc. List the company name, policy numbers, and contact information. Monthly Budget: Include a copy of your monthly budget to help your family keep track of bills and run your household once you are gone. Passwords: If you’re like most people, you have probably have a large and growing list of passwords, usernames and PIN numbers for your bank accounts, web sites, voicemail, and more. Make a list of these important access codes in a single file. Spiritual Will: A “love letter” from you expressing your love for Christ and your family, and communicating your values, life lessons and beliefs. Tax Returns: It is recommended that you keep up to 7 years of tax returns on file in the event that you are audited by the IRS. This precaution will spare your family from a lot of unnecessary hassle if you are no longer around. Will: A signed copy of your Will, including information about guardianship, beneficiaries, executor, power of attorney, financial accounts, and charitable interests. Request Your Brochure Now Request Your Free Brochure Fill out this form below to receive our latest Legacy Giving informational resources designed to inform and inspire you on your journey to discovering the joy and benefits of creating a legacy gift. Open the online form Legacy Giving FAQ Now that you have a basic idea of what you need to do to create your Will, here are some additional resources to help answer any questions you may have: How do I include the Mission’s work in my Will? Here are the most common ways to significantly increase your ministry impact through your Will: Add “Ministry” to your family: Some families treat ministry organizations like an additional child. For example, if a family has three children, they might add a fourth child named “Ministry” and divide the assets in their Will into four equal parts. Each of their children would receive 25%, and the remaining 25% would be divided among their favorite ministry organizations. Tithe on your Estate: Other families commit a 10% tithe of their estate to the ministry organizations they love, dividing the remaining 90% among their heirs. Add a “Cap” to your Will: Others prayerfully decide to “cap” their children’s inheritance, leaving the rest of their assets to ministry. This approach is used when the parents want to provide a modest gift to bless their children and eliminate concerns of creating dependence or giving too much too soon. Update an existing Will: An attorney can add, delete or change an item in your Will with an additional statement called a “codicil.” Here’s an example: “I give, devise, and bequeath twenty-five percent (25%) of my residuary estate to [church or ministry name] whose address is [city, state, zip code]. Like a Will, a codicil must be dated, signed and witnessed. How do online Wills work? Most Online Will sites guide you through a simple 3-step process: Answer Questions: You’ll be guided through a series of fill-in-the-blank questions about your wishes regarding your family, your property, who you want to be in charge of making sure your wishes are taken care of. The questionnaire is often provided at no charge, and most people can complete it within about 30 minutes. Review Answers: You’ll have an opportunity to review your own answers for completeness and accuracy. Some sites also provide online tools and “ask a lawyer” features to give you a more in-depth review. Finalize Documents: The last step is to receive your documents online or in the mail. The Online Will site will also provide instructions for getting signatures to finalize your documents, as well as storage recommendations. Do I need a lawyer to make a Will? No. There is no legal requirement that a Will be drawn up by a lawyer. Most people can use quality, fill-in-the-blank legal documents to take care of basic concerns such as leaving their property to loved ones and naming a guardian for young children. However, there are a number of situations where it would be highly recommended to work with a lawyer instead of an Online Will: If you have significant assets. If you have a special needs, disabled or dependent adult child. If you’ve been divorced or remarried. If you think one of your heirs might contest your Will. If you own a small business. If you are concerned about guardianship issues for minor children. If you’re raising grandchildren or stepchildren. If you or your spouse are citizens of another country. If you have questions about your Will or the Online form doesn’t address your situation. How do I find a Christian Estate Planning Attorney? If you decide to use a lawyer to create or update your Will—or review your Online Will—you’ll want to find an attorney who shares your Christian values and is knowledgeable in estate planning. There are 3 sources you can check for a referral to a trusted Christian estate planning attorney: Contact Us: You can contact our office or Orchard Alliance for a referral. Christian Legal Society: You can go online for a referral from the Christian Legal Society, a national network of approximately 3,000 legal professionals committed to loving and serving Jesus Christ in the practice of law. Your Pastor: Your Pastor is probably connected to a wide network of people, which may include a Christian estate planning attorney. Even if he doesn’t know a Christian attorney, he can ask others for a trusted referral because of his position. What are the advantages of an Online Will? Is an online Will right for you? Below are four reasons people get an Online Will: Affordable: Let’s face it. When it comes to getting a Will, cost is a big concern for many people. A lawyer may charge you $500 for a basic Will (and a lot more if your estate is complicated). But most people can get an Online Will for less than $70. Easy: Online Will sites provide simple questionnaires that the average person can answer in about 30 minutes or less. With an attorney, you may have to schedule a couple of face-to-face appointments to review your information and to finalize your documents. Quality: Do-it-yourself online legal documents have been accepted by court and government agencies in all 50 states. Some of the most popular Online Will sites were started by attorneys—and offer high-quality, legally valid, state-specific Wills. Private: Some people are uncomfortable with the idea of discussing their financial and family information with a complete stranger. Although attorneys are required to keep your discussions confidential, many prefer the anonymity of fill-in-the-blank online forms. I already have a gift to the Mission planned in my Will or estate. Do you need to know the details about it? While you don’t have to inform us of your legacy gift ahead of time, letting us know about it does help us plan better for the future and show you our appreciation. Legacy Giving donors who set up a gift for us in their Will or estate become part of our Goodheart Society , named after a former, influential Mission director from nearly 100 years ago. If you do want to inform us of your legacy gift plans, simply send us a Notice of Bequest to get started. Send a Notice of Bequest If you are creating a legacy gift to the Mission, you may need our EIN number: 84-6038762 . Explore Ways to Give We partner with Orchard Alliance to assist you with a wide variety of more complex planned giving options. Click the link below if you are interested in learning more about asset-based giving that may help reduce your or your family’s tax burden, as well as other charitable giving tools – including a Charitable Gift Annuity, which provides you with a dependable stream of income during your lifetime. title: Tax Credit Programs
description: Important Update: Homeless Contribution Tax Credit Approved Through 2030
text: Ways To Give Homeless Contribution Tax Credit Important Update: Homeless Contribution Tax Credit Approved Through 2030 Denver Rescue Mission is a participant in Colorado’s Homeless Contribution Tax Credit (HCTC) , which is available statewide for a broad range of homelessness response-related activities. Through HCTC, qualifying donors may receive a Colorado state income tax credit equal to 25% of their eligible donation . This applies to individual gifts of $250 or more in cash or more than $5,000 in qualifying in-kind donations , such as stocks, bonds or other eligible gifts. To issue the tax credit certificate, Denver Rescue Mission is required to have the last four digits of the donor’s Social Security Number on file. If you have received HCTC for a past gift, no further action is needed. You do not need to submit your SSN again or “renew” your participation. Denver Rescue Mission will continue applying HCTC to your eligible gifts as long as you make a qualifying gift, tax credits remain available, you remain a Colorado resident, or you have not stated that you no longer wish to receive HCTC. If your SSN has already been provided, your HCTC certificate will be sent by the State of Colorado through encrypted email at a later date. Gifts made through intermediary organizations, such as Mile High United Way and Colorado Gives, may also qualify. To learn more about Colorado’s Homeless Contribution Tax Credit, visit the state’s website . Please note: The State limits the number of credits available to each participating organization each calendar year. Consult with your professional tax adviser to determine whether the HCTC program will benefit your specific tax situation. Ready to Make a Qualifying Gift? Have questions? Need to make changes? Contact Us How HCTC Donations Work Homeless Contribution Tax Credits allows a dollar-for-dollar reduction in state taxes owed by an amount equal to 25% of cash donations to Denver Rescue Mission of $250 or more or $5,000 or more for in-kind donations (stocks). 1. Give a Gift of $250 or more. Monetary donations that are individual gifts of $250 or more or $5,000 or more for in-kind donations (stocks). (Certain limitations apply. Learn more here. ) 2. Tell us you want HCTC tax credit. You must indicate your desire for Homeless Contribution Tax Credit. For example, write “HCTC” on the memo line of your check. Or, when donating online, write “HCTC” in the donor comments section. If your SSN has been obtained previously, your certificate will be sent by the State through an encrypted email later. If you are a new donor to HCTC or you have not given your last four of your SSN to DRM previously, please call us at 303.313.2422 to provide one of the following: Federal Employer Tax Identification Number (FEIN) Or the Last Four Digits of a Social Security Number (this is a State requirement for the HCTC program). Please do not include your SSN in an online gift comment, email, or voicemail message. To provide your SSN securely, please call us at 303.313.2422 between 9 AM and 5 PM (Monday – Friday) and speak with a representative directly. 3. Receive your gift receipt and tax credit certificate. First, within 7-14 days you will receive a tax receipt in the mail from the Mission. This is separate from the HCTC tax credit certificate. Then, based on current processing guidelines set by the State, HCTC certificates will be emailed out on a rolling basis, and could take 6-8 weeks (or longer during busy periods) from the time the Mission receives a qualified gift and the last four digits of a SSN from the donor. This timeline is subject to change. You will receive an electronic version of the tax credit certificate(s) with the subject line: DOLA HCTC Program, which may go to your Junk/Spam mail. You must file your tax return electronically with the Colorado Department of Revenue. HCTC Limitations According to the Colorado Department of Local Affairs (DOLA), the State entity that manages the new Homeless Contribution Tax Credit Program, donations made through workplace giving programs facilitated by third-party organizations like Benevity and other intermediary or “pass-through” organizations like Donor Advised Funds (DAFs) will not be eligible for the 25% HCTC tax credit. Gifts made directly by your employer (excluding Benevity) or handled through a payment processor or donation software platform to Denver Rescue Mission on your behalf would still qualify. With the passing of legislation on June 7th, 2024, DOLA now allows donations made through intermediary organizations such as Mile High United Way and the Colorado Gives Foundation will now qualify under the guidelines stated above. Please reference the State’s FAQ document and other resources below for more details. Additionally, check with your employer to verify your workplace giving process prior to making a donation to ensure a gift qualifies. HCTC Resources For your convenience, we’ve gathered several HCTC resources here that can help you learn more about the program and how it may apply to your donations. title: Vehicle Donations
description: Donate your car, truck, motorcycle, or other vehicle today!
text: Ways To Give Give A Vehicle Donate your car, truck, motorcycle, or other vehicle today! When you donate a car, we’ll fix it up and either give it directly to program graduates or sell it to support Mission programs and services. For many people, owning a vehicle is a huge step toward independence. Furthermore, it can save time and money for individuals and families coming out of poverty and homelessness, and provide stability and increased opportunities. Get Started Now Need help or have questions? Call us at 303.331.2938 What Type of Car Can I Donate? We accept vehicles in any condition. Cars, trucks or other donated vehicles that need moderate repairs are ideal, but we also accept cars that are not running and even some vehicles you may think are “junk.” Cars that cannot be repaired and/or gifted for any reason can still be used to support Mission programs and services, so please contact us with any questions. Still wonder if your vehicle is good to donate? Don’t worry. Contact us today at 303.331.2938 to see how you can donate your car. Benefits of Donating a Car When you donate your car to Denver Rescue Mission, you’re providing independence and transportation to someone who has worked hard for months in one of our programs to overcome homelessness and poverty. For someone who has lost everything, your car could be the difference that helps them be able to keep their new job, care for their children, make it on time to necessary appointments, and more. And you’ll benefit too! All donated vehicles, regardless of condition, are tax-deductible. So instead of junking a car for a couple hundred dollars, donate your vehicle to receive more value for your tax-deductible gift. Donate a Car Today It’s easy, free and tax deductible. Every vehicle donation situation is unique, but the best way to get started is to contact us. Start by sending us some details about your vehicle, and we’ll get in touch with you to answer any questions. Get Started Now Your Vehicle Can Change Lives! “My job during my stay at The Crossing was a mechanic for the Vehicle Program. I worked in the Shop for over a year and I have firsthand experience of the joy a vehicle can bring to a person’s life. Many people would break down in tears when they receive their vehicle.” Mike “My daughter and I are so grateful to have a reliable vehicle. We are members of a church and it is important to us to be active members but we were limited by transportation. Even getting to family events presented its challenges. It’s not easy asking people for a ride or limiting the time you can spend in one place because of public transportation. If I could convey one thing to the vehicle donors its, your donation makes a difference.” Barry “Writing the Thank You card to the donor was a great part of receiving my vehicle. It was so nice to be able to tell that person what their donation was going to do for our lives. It was approaching winter season and I remember being so overjoyed that my son and I wouldn’t be at the bus stop in the cold. I was also thrilled that I no longer needed to plan for a two hour commute as well.” Donna News & Stories Stay connected. Connect with us to get the latest news from Denver Rescue Mission. title: Homelessness in Denver

text: What We Do No Place to Call Home The Faces and Families Behind Homelessness With data continuing to emerge regarding Denver’s housing market, nationwide drug-abuse epidemics and other factors contributing to chronic homelessness, it is clear that many individuals are still facing uncertainty when it comes to food, shelter and safety. 10,774 people are experiencing homelessness in the Denver Metro area 80% seek shelter with organizations like Denver Rescue Mission to stay safe overnight 30% are struggling families, many experiencing homelessness for the first time 34% have experienced chronic homelessness (1 year + or multiple times in several years) 20% of the total homeless population in Metro Denver are unsheltered, living on the streets, in cars, in abandoned buildings, under bridges, or camping in open areas. HELP NOW Statistics provided by Metro Denver Homeless Initiative: mdhi.org/pit Causes and Barriers Homelessness is a complex issue that affects many people in cities across the country, and Denver is no exception. Some of the challenges facing those experiencing homelessness include: Lack of affordable housing: Denver’s housing market has become increasingly expensive, making it difficult for low-income individuals and families to find affordable housing as well as keep up with rising rents and mortgage payments. Chronic health conditions: Disabling conditions or injuries and lack of access to proper healthcare can lead to further mental and physical health concerns which may affect employment status and ability to maintain stable housing. Domestic violence: Individuals attempting to escape domestic abuse or hostile environments may be able to remove themselves from the abuse or the environment but may find themselves with lack of support or resources to rebuild their lives after, which in turn could lead to homelessness. Job Loss: The high cost of living in Denver combined with limited job opportunities and low wages can leave individuals facing unemployment and their families struggling to make ends meet. Substance abuse: With the opioid epidemic leaving many in a crippling cycle of addiction, without access to proper treatment or services, many find it extremely difficult to obtain stability and break the cycle. Creating Lasting Change Changing lives for the long term is only possible by helping people identify the root causes of homelessness in their lives, and helping them address them. At Denver Rescue Mission, we are committed to helping people through the transformative love of Jesus Christ. See how lives are restored News & Stories Stay connected. text: What We Do How We Help Denver Rescue Mission is changing lives in the name of Christ by meeting people at their physical and spiritual points of need with the goal of returning them to society as productive, self-sufficient citizens. Five connected strategies Prevention, Dignity, Recovery, Readiness, and Housing guide our work. Programs put these strategies into practice, and a single program can support more than one strategy. Prevention Sometimes the most important step toward stability happens before someone ever loses their home. Dignity A welcoming place. A listening ear. The respect every neighbor deserves. Dignity is the foundation of how we meet people, wherever their journey begins. Recovery For people navigating addiction, trauma, and other difficult circumstances, change takes time. Recovery is built through relationships, support, and the opportunity to move forward—one step at a time. Readiness Lasting stability takes more than a single opportunity. It takes preparation, confidence, relationships, and practical tools to move forward. Housing A safe, stable place to call home changes what is possible. Our work connects neighbors with support as they seek housing—and as they build a foundation for what comes next. Our programs and services Prevention In partnership with public schools, one-time financial assistance and case management help families at risk of losing their housing. Bridge & Family Shelter At The Crossing, Bridge gives men, women and families a safe place to live while working toward stable housing. Food Pantry & Household Items The Ministry Outreach Center provides food, clothing, hygiene items and household essentials. Daytime Services The Lawrence Street Community Center provides meals, drinking water, restrooms and connections to support. New Life Program A residential program for men seeking recovery, life skills, employment and sustainable housing. CAPs Commodity Assistance Partners are approved nonprofits that receive items to support people in need. Overnight Shelter Nightly shelter for men, with bed assignments coordinated through the Lawrence Street Community Center. Pathways of Life Recovery Clinical outpatient substance use treatment through Pathways of Life Recovery Services, a Denver Rescue Mission subsidiary. Need help? text: Who We Are Frequently Asked Questions What does Denver Rescue Mission do? Denver Rescue Mission meets the needs of those experiencing poverty and homelessness through emergency services, rehabilitation programs, transitional programs, and community outreach. Since 1892, the Mission has been changing lives in our community. If you or a loved one needs help, click Get Help or call 303.297.1815. Where is Denver Rescue Mission located? We have five different locations throughout Denver and two in northern Colorado. Each location serves a unique and vital role in helping address the issues related to homelessness and in helping those experiencing homelessness return to society as productive, self-sufficient citizens. You can learn more about our locations here . How do I volunteer at Denver Rescue Mission? Volunteers are the life-blood of Denver Rescue Mission. Short-term and long-term opportunities are available, including serving meals, sorting clothing, becoming a mentor, and more! Becoming a volunteer is easy. Simply visit our Volunteer page, create a volunteer profile and choose a serving shift and facility that works with your schedule. (We do ask that you sign up to volunteer on our website and not show up unannounced.) For more information, call our volunteer hotline at 303.953.3955. Can I donate online? Monetary donations can be made online , by mail or by phone. Does Denver Rescue Mission participate in any door-to-door solicitation? Denver Rescue Mission does not support, partner or benefit from any individuals or companies claiming to raise funds through door-to-door solicitations. If you have any questions of our involvement in a fundraising program, please contact us at 303.297.1815. What types of gift-in-kind donations (items) do you accept? The Mission always needs non-perishable food, clothing, hygiene items, furniture, and household items. Learn More Do you pick up donations? We offer free pickups for furniture and large items. We do not pick up clothing, food or household items unless they are in addition to a piece of furniture or a large item. Learn more about scheduling a furniture pickup here . What is Denver Rescue Mission’s Tax I.D. #? The Mission’s tax I.D. number is 84-6038762. Does Denver Rescue Mission provide rental assistance? The Mission’s Bridge Program provides transitional housing at The Crossing, and our Pathway Home program provides assistance for permanent housing as well as community mentoring and connection. These are the only transitional and assistance programs available. Learn how to Get Help here . Does Denver Rescue Mission provide assistance with utilities? No. Please contact your local city/county for assistance programs. How can I receive assistance with food and clothing? The Client Services department at our Ministry Outreach Center provides a wide range of community outreach services including a food pantry and clothing while also offering emotional and spiritual support. VIEW ALL LOCATIONS Donating to Denver Rescue Mission Managing Donations Through WeGive How do I access my donor account to manage my donations? I’m an online, Pathways of Hope monthly donor, how do I manage/modify my monthly giving plan? I mailed a check, but it’s not been cashed yet. What should I do? Due to COVID-19 safety and social distancing protocols, our donation processing is currently experiencing delays. Please know we are working as quickly and as safely as possible to process your gift and send you a receipt. Thank you for your patience and understanding. If you have any further questions, please contact us . How can I make an online donation to Denver Rescue Mission? Donations are easy to complete online. You can give my card, bank account, PayPal, Venmo, and popular digital wallets. DONATE NOW How will I know my donation was completed? When you make an online donation, you will receive an email confirmation message once your donation is complete. Receipts will also be mailed to the address you have provided within 7-10 business days for gifts $5 or greater. L ogin to access your donor account. My credit card was rejected. What should I do? We use a secure payment processor to ensure that your credit card information is safe. Sometimes the payment processor may reject your information for unspecified reasons. If the charge has been blocked on your bank statement, we recommend contacting your issuing bank to understand why the charge was blocked. You can also call us at 303.297.1815 to donate securely over the phone. Is my online donation processed securely? Protecting your online security when you make a donation is our top priority. Denver Rescue Mission uses industry-leading Secure Sockets Layer (SSL) technology to keep your personal information as secure as possible and protect against the loss, misuse and alteration of the information you entrust to us. We protect your information by working with partners that provide a secure and safe environment for credit card donations. All information is stored in a secure database. For more information, view our Privacy Policy and Terms of Use . Is my donation tax deductible?​ Donations made to Denver Rescue Mission are 100% tax deductible to the full extent permitted by law. The Mission is a registered 501(c)3 charitable organization (EIN: 84-6038762). We issue tax receipts at the time of donation. If you would like to request a receipt for one or more donations you made this year, please contact us or access your online donor account . Some Mission events may include a registration fee, which is often either not tax deductible, or only partially tax deductible. Please consult with your tax advisor for proper tax treatment of any donations How can I change or update my credit card information? If you are a monthly donor, you can update your donation credit card details on our donor login portal . If you would like to change or update your credit card information over the phone, please call 303.297.1815 and we will be happy to assist you. If you do not have a recurring gift set up, our third-party partners do not retain your credit card details. Denver Rescue Mission does not retain credit card numbers for any online donations. Recurring donations are processed by a trusted third-party vendor who meets Level 1 PCI compliance standards. Read our Privacy Policy for details. How can I change or cancel my donation? You can make adjustments to your donation by calling us at 303.297.1815. Monthly donors can adjust their giving plans on our donor account portal . Where does my donation go? When you give to Denver Rescue Mission, you want to know that your gifts are really making a difference. That’s why we’re committed to helping you understand the real impact of your donations and how your gifts help change lives. See our Financial Accountability page for more details on how your donation has made an impact in our community. Can I donate by mail? Yes, gifts can be received through the mail. Please mail your donation to the following address: Denver Rescue Mission PO Box 5206 Denver, CO 80217 The Mission does not recommend sending cash through the mail. How can I change my mailing address?​ To change your mailing address, please call 303.297.1815 or contact us online. How can I update my mailing preferences?​ Our mailings are one of the ways we report back to our donors about the lives changed because of their support, and they are an important way we receive gifts from our supporters. Often, these mailers serve as a reminder that we need our supporters’ help throughout the year and, without them, we would be unable to continue providing food, shelter and life-changing programs to people in need. If you want to reduce or change the number of mailings you receive, we’re happy to help. Simply call us at 303.297.1815 or contact us online to update your mail preferences. Any change will take 8-12 weeks to take effect. News & Stories Stay connected. Connect with us to get the latest news from Denver Rescue Mission. Sign up for emails
